questions.question:
The StatefulSet `web` in the namespace `stateful` runs `3` replicas of `nginx:1.25`.

Roll out `nginx:1.27` **only to the Pod `web-2`** for now, using the StatefulSet's rolling-update partition. `web-0` and `web-1` must keep running `nginx:1.25`. Do not delete any Pod yourself.

The Deployment `frontend` in the namespace `frontend` reads its settings from the **immutable** ConfigMap `frontend-config-v1` (`LOG_LEVEL=info`).

Switch it to debug logging: create the immutable ConfigMap `frontend-config-v2` with `LOG_LEVEL=debug` and `THEME=dark`, and make `frontend` use it instead of `frontend-config-v1`. Do not delete `frontend-config-v1` (it is kept for a rollback).

verification.description: frontend-config-v2 is immutable with the new data, v1 kept
frontend uses frontend-config-v2 and logs debug

questions.question:
In the namespace `telemetry`, create a Pod `meta-reporter` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'env; sleep 3600'`) with a memory limit of `64Mi`, which exposes the following values as environment variables through the **Downward API**:

- `POD_NAME`: the Pod name
- `POD_IP`: the Pod IP
- `NODE_NAME`: the name of the node it runs on
- `MEM_LIMIT_MI`: its own memory limit, in mebibytes (the value must be `64`)

verification.description: Environment variables come from the Downward API

questions.question:
The Pods of the Deployment `api` in the namespace `startup` stay in `Init:0/1`. The init container is meant to wait until the database Service of the namespace can be resolved, but the database Service is running fine.

Find the cause and fix the **Deployment** (the Service `database` must not be changed) so that the `api` Pods start.

verification.description: The init container waits for the right Service, which is unchanged

questions.question:
Applications in the namespace `payments` must reach the external provider `api.payments-provider.example.com` under the in-cluster name `provider`.

Create a Service `provider` in `payments` that returns a DNS `CNAME` to that host (no proxying, no endpoints).

In the namespace `crawler`, create a NetworkPolicy `crawler-egress` for the Pods labeled `app=crawler` that allows egress **only** to:

- the network `10.20.0.0/16`, **except** `10.20.5.0/24`, on TCP ports `8000` to `8100` (one port range)
- DNS (UDP and TCP port `53`) to any destination

Ingress must not be affected.

The Deployment `cache` in the namespace `cache` runs `3` Redis-like Pods (label `app=cache`, port `6379`). Clients need the IP of **every** Pod, not a single virtual IP.

1. Create a **headless** Service `cache-peers` in `cache` for these Pods, with a port named `redis` (`6379`)
2. Write the fully-qualified DNS name of that Service to `/tmp/exam/q7/fqdn.txt` on `cka-q7`

verification.description: cache-peers is headless and selects the cache Pods

questions.question:
In the namespace `ci`:

1. Create the ServiceAccount `builder` that does **not** automatically mount its API token into Pods
2. Create a Pod `builder` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) that runs as `builder`, and receives a token for the audience `vault` valid `3600` seconds through a **projected** volume, as the file `/var/run/secrets/vault/token`

The default API token must not be mounted in the Pod.

verification.description: Pod builder has only the projected vault token

questions.question:
The user `jane` must be able to read and change **only** the ConfigMap `app-settings` in the namespace `config`, and no other ConfigMap.

Create the Role `app-settings-editor` (verbs `get`, `update`, `patch`) and the RoleBinding `jane-app-settings` in `config`. `jane` must not be able to list, create or delete ConfigMaps.

verification.description: jane has exactly the requested access

questions.question:
In the namespace `secure`, create a Pod `hardened` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'while true; do date >> /work/log; sleep 10; done'`) that:

- runs as user `1000`, group `3000`, and uses `fsGroup` `2000`
- has a **read-only** root filesystem
- cannot escalate privileges and drops **all** Linux capabilities
- writes to an `emptyDir` volume mounted at `/work`

verification.description: The Pod runs and can only write to /work

questions.question:
When a node becomes unreachable, Kubernetes evicts its Pods after `300` seconds by default. The Deployment `edge-cache` in the namespace `edge` must move faster.

Change `edge-cache` so its Pods are evicted **30 seconds** after their node gets the `NoExecute` taint `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable` or `node.kubernetes.io/not-ready`.

verification.description: The running Pods carry the new tolerations

questions.question:
A fast disk is mounted at `/mnt/disks/ssd1` on the node `k3d-cluster-agent-1` only.

1. Create the StorageClass `local-ssd` with the provisioner `kubernetes.io/no-provisioner` and binding mode `WaitForFirstConsumer`
2. Create the PersistentVolume `ssd-pv-1` (`2Gi`, `ReadWriteOnce`, reclaim policy `Retain`, class `local-ssd`) of type **`local`** for that path, usable only on `k3d-cluster-agent-1`
3. Create the PVC `ssd-claim` in the namespace `localdisk` requesting `2Gi` of `local-ssd`

No Pod uses the claim yet, so it is expected to stay `Pending`.

verification.description: ssd-pv-1 is a local PV pinned to k3d-cluster-agent-1

questions.question:
The Deployment `checkout` in the namespace `checkout` has been updated several times and the current version is broken.

1. Find the revision of `checkout` that ran `nginx:1.25` and write its number to `/tmp/exam/q13/revision.txt` on `cka-q13`
2. Roll `checkout` back to **that** revision (not just the previous one)

verification.description: revision.txt has the revision number of nginx:1.25

questions.question: Write the list of **distinct** container images used by the Pods in the namespace `inventory` to `/tmp/exam/q14/images.txt` on `cka-q14`: one image per line, sorted alphabetically, no duplicates. Include init containers.

In the namespace `gw-lab`, the Gateway `public` (class `ckx-gateway`) and the Services `api-stable` and `api-beta` (port `8080`) already exist. There is no gateway controller, so only the resources are graded.

Create an HTTPRoute `api` attached to `public` for the hostname `api.example.local`:

- requests with the header `x-channel: beta` go to `api-beta`
- all other requests go to `api-stable`

verification.description: HTTPRoute api routes x-channel: beta to api-beta, the rest to api-stable

questions.question:
The Service `orders` in the namespace `orders` has no endpoints although the Pods of the Deployment `orders` are running, and clients get `connection refused`.

Fix the **Service** (not the Deployment) so that it sends port `80` traffic to the `orders` Pods.

verification.description: Service selector and targetPort fixed, Deployment unchanged
orders has ready endpoints on port 80
